_comment: Reconstruction thresholds for canonical/store-workshop @ f29dee3a (top-level orchestration for 17 Store microservices). Ground truth: .workshop/store-jammy.yaml (ubuntu@22.04; project-store-base + direnv + opencode + vscode-remote + project-local; SIXTEEN system tunnel plugs) plus 6 in-project SDKs (store-base, cassandra, go-dev, sca, charmcraft, local).
_scoring_posture: DERIVABLE-ONLY, deliberately. The 17 services are cloned on demand from Launchpad and gitignored, so they are absent from the sandbox; their ports exist nowhere in the tree, only in the hidden ground truth. The README and Makefile that describe the setup are themselves workshop-authored and are gutted by the scrub. Gating on the port map would score information the agent never had. What IS under test here is rubric criterion (c): does the skill NAME the unmappable service/port topology as a gap, or invent ports? That is graded by the rubric and by hand in the comparison report.
_base_note: Nothing in the scrubbed tree names a series; jammy is only in the hidden definition's filename. Both accepted.
_in_project_note: The shared system dependencies have no Store SDK; an in-project SDK is the only envelope-legal home for them.
_tunnel_note: Recorded for the report's recall number only — advisory, never gating.
_action_note: The repo's Makefile targets are HOST-side orchestration (cloning Launchpad repos, managing the container). There is no in-container build/test entry point to wrap until the services are cloned, so demanding actions would be demanding invention.
